research_question: Whether replacing the separate anchor W1 addmm and u@A by one [W1,A] addmm changes measured whole-generation latency or BF16 trajectory for this exact exposed source, while retaining G19 nonlinear anchor and BF16 C.

hypotheses_with_opposing_predictions.prediction: Shared input and fewer GEMM dispatches improve repeated whole-generation latency with unchanged observed full-video identity.
Wide layout, GEMM algorithm choice, temporary allocation and native offload overlap remove the speed benefit or alter BF16 outputs.

adversarial_counterexample: A wide GEMM can select a different reduction algorithm: a one-ULP change in W1 preactivation or q changes GELU, C and subsequent hit trajectory. High/low layer-0 probes can agree while another layer differs; this defeats a claim of universal bitwise equivalence. Equally, fewer logical GEMMs can be slower because of unfavorable wide shape and row stride.

constraints: Single exact scope and one attempt. Approval is not ACTIVE registration or evidence of actual execution; root must prelaunch-check remote identities and queue before serialized submit.

Dispatcher counts jobs rather than allocated GPU TRES and has no cross-process lock; approval relies on root confirmed serialized submission and all session jobs one GPU. No concurrent independent dispatch allowed.

Mean ratio alone is insufficient evidence of improvement; use all four ordered pair timings and direction stability. Whole-generate includes noise hash and encoding overhead equally; no clean FFN-only latency estimate is produced.

Old G0 timing is descriptive only. Same packed-residency baseline isolates fusion and is not the memory-minimal original implementation. Report extra packing/setup and 14.45GiB packed payload separately.
